notes.title: 1.0.6.13 Beta Release!
notes.content:
Dear PGMMV Users,

Thank you for your continued support of PGMMV!
Version 1.0.6.13 is now available for download via the Beta channel!
In addition to a few fixes, there are 2 functions being added with 1.0.6.13. 
The first is the addition of Invincibility duration to the Received Damage settings. This will allow configuration of different invincibility times based on which type of element hits the Object, making invincibility a much more flexible feature to use.
The second new feature affects Fields of Vision. Previously, they had a fixed direction and would not change based on Object orientation. With 1.0.6.13, Fields of Vision will now update according to an Objects orientation. This should make all kinds of functionality much easier to implement, for top or side view games!

[h2]Ver. 1.0.6.13 (Beta) Release Notes[/h2]
[h3]Editor[/h3]
[list]
[*]Added Invincibility configuration settings to the Received Damage settings.
[/list]
[h3]Player[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fields of Vision now rotate to follow Object orientation.
[*] Fixed a bug that could cause child Objects to lose track of the parent’s instance ID after a portal is used when the parent is the Player.
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent bullet Objects from functioning correctly when set to use the “Shoot at the Selected On-Screen Object Group(s)” setting in some situations.
[/list]
To apply this Beta version please change the branch to 1.0.6-beta via the Steam library.
Also, we remind users participating in the Nintendo Switch publishing program to continue using the 1.0.6-switch-beta branch when working on Switch builds.
[How to Change Branch]
[h3]Caution: We strongly recommend backing up your project before attempting the following. [/h3]
1.Go to Steam Library, right click "Pixel Game Maker MV" and select "Properties".
2.Click on the "Beta" tab, select the target version from the Beta Participation menu and close "Properties".

[Reverting Back to Default]
Follow the instructions below to switch from the Beta version back to the previous version.
1.Go to Steam Library, right click "Pixel Game Maker MV" and select "Properties".
2.Select "None" for Beta Participation and close "Properties".
Please continue enjoying your game dev life with PGMMV!

notes.title: Changes to the Nintendo Switch Publishing Service for Pixel Game Maker MV
notes.content:
Thank you for your support of Pixel Game Maker MV!
We have an important announcement regarding the Nintendo Switch Publishing service that Gotcha Gotcha Games has been offering.

Launched on May 15th, 2021, we’ve been able to release more than 50 different games on the Nintendo Switch as of November, 2024. We are very grateful to every developer who has participated, and it was one of the main attractions for developers using Pixel Game Maker MV.

For those interested, you can take a look at the list of games published via this service here:
[url=https://rpgmakerofficial.com/act_game/?lang=en]https://rpgmakerofficial.com/act_game/?lang=en[/url]

However, it has been 7 years since Pixel Game Maker MV was released. There’s been a lot of changes in hardware, consumer expectations towards game development tools, and even the release of new console generations.
In order to rise to meet those changes, we’ve developed the much improved successor, ACTION GAME MAKER, which will be released in 2025.

We can confirm that ACTION GAME MAKER will support porting to most active consoles, including the Nintendo Switch.

Please read about console support for ACTION GAME MAKER here:
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2987180/view/4687773573366304993]https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2987180/view/4687773573366304993[/url]

Due to these various reasons, the Pixel Game Maker MV Nintendo Switch publishing service will be reduced as of April 1st, 2025. This will not impact any functions in Pixel Game Maker MV, and user support will continue with not change.

For developers wishing to publish their Pixel Game Maker MV but that have not applied for Nintendo Switch publishing access, you will need to apply by March 31, 2025. Additionally, games must pass through Nintendo’s approval process no later than March 31, 2026. Note that from initial contracting phase through completing Nintendo’s approval process takes at least 10 weeks, best effort. So please keep that in mind if you intend to apply.

[h2]Schedule of Changes[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/252995147bd8c70692b5c59b9cf841d47d43e104.jpg[/img]

(1)While new applications will cease from this date, developers with pre-existing contracts will retain full access to Switch functionality until the 2026-3-31 date.
(2)Access to the Nintendo Switch development tools for Pixel Game Maker MV will cease to be provided from this date. Released titles will remain on sale.
 
[h2]Best Effort Timeline For Release[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/13f6efed45724d77eb6dd700b42de890659de9e3.jpg[/img]								
[b]Step 8, Lot Check Approval, must be completed by 2026-03-31[/b]

As stated above, it takes an estimated 10 weeks to complete lot check approval best effort. Larger games or those with many issues found in the debug process will require more time, and this schedule assumes receiving approval on first lot check submission. Failing the initial lot check submission will add multiple weeks to the required time. Please keep this in mind when preparing your production plan.

[h3]Application Process[/h3]
[url=https://rpgmakerofficial.com/en/application/action_tkool/]https://rpgmakerofficial.com/en/application/action_tkool/[/url]
Please use the above link if you wish to proceed with a Pixel Game Maker MV submission before the deadline approaches. However, if your game looks like it will not be ready before the deadline we suggest to our community that they consider moving their project to ACTION GAME MAKER upon its release.

[h2]Moving a Project to ACTION GAME MAKER[/h2]
ACTION GAME MAKER uses the Godot Engine, which was not used in Pixel Game Maker MV. Due to this difference, a direct import function will not be provided.
That said, ACTION GAME MAKER supports the same Runtime Action system used by Pixel Game Maker MV, so recreating the logic should be a mostly simple process. However, due to the change in engine, there may be some unintended side effects, so please keep that in mind. Also, most resources (file types) are supported by ACTION GAME MAKER MV, though configuring settings after importing will be required.

[h2]Supported Resource Data[/h2]
*Audio Files (Music/SFX)
*Sprite Sheets/Tile Maps/Backgrounds/Fonts/Image Files
File Conversion Required
*Video Files: Conversion to Ogg Theora is required before videos can be used.
Not Supported
*OPTPIX Sprite Studio sspj format and GIF animations are not supported. Use of Godot’s Animation Player will be required to recreate the motions.
*Particle Effects: Particle effects will need to be recreated using GPUParticles2D and CPUParticles2D, which are Godot Engine functions.
 
Additional information can be found on the ACTION GAME MAKER Steam page and in the Producer Letters we have released, so please check them out!
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2987180/ACTION_GAME_MAKER/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/2987180/ACTION_GAME_MAKER/[/url]
 
We most sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this will cause on all Pixel Game Maker MV developers who were considering a Nintendo Switch release, and ask for your understanding.

Please contact us at
pgmmv-support@gotchagotcha.jp 
If you have any questions about the changes outlined above.

notes.title: Releasing Stable Version 1.0.6.12!
notes.content:
Hello dear PGM users!
Thank you for your continued support of Pixel Game Maker MV!
We have now formally released the default stable branch version 1.0.6.12.
Stable version updates are distributed automatically to all users. For users who wish to stay in the previous Ver1.0.6.3, please follow the instruction [How to Change Branch] at the bottom and change to version 1.0.6 – legacy.

With the release of 1.0.6.12, as with the current main branch, it will not be possible to access the Nintendo Switch functions properly. To address this, users who need access to Nintendo Switch functionality will be asked to try the 1.0.6-switch beta branch.

[h2]stable version 1.0.6.12 release note[/h2]
[h3]Editor[/h3]
[list]
[*]Added new Option: enables selection for specific versions to use for the Player, Runtime, and Debugging Runtime components.
[*]Fixed issue that could cause a crash when trying to do an encrypted build of a project with a large file size.
[*]Fixed issue when displaying particles on the menu layer which could prevent the connection point from being acquired.
[/list]

[h3]Player[/h3]
[list]
[*]Improved display options for the F1 debug menu.
[*]Fixed a texture display issue caused by using the F1 debug menu to forcibly change languages.
[*]Fixed issue that could cause saved data to be generated in an unintended location.
[*]Fixed issue that caused the “Apply Damage Rate to Parent” option for Child Objects to not work properly.
[*]Fixed issue where GIF animations do not display properly after scaling is changed.
[*]Fixed issue preventing WebM format videos from playing properly.
[*]Added the "Controller Settings" F1 menu item. It allows changing of the active controller.
[*]The amount of memory that can be handled by the player component has been increased from 2GB to 4 GB.
[/list]

[How to Change Branch] 
[h3] Caution: We strongly recommend backing up your project before attempting the following. [/h3]
1. Go to Steam Library, right click "Pixel Game Maker MV" and select "Properties".
2. Click on the "Beta" tab, select correct version and close "Properties".

[Reverting Back to Default]
Follow the instructions below to switch from the Beta version back to the previous version.
1. Go to Steam Library, right click "Pixel Game Maker MV" and select "Properties".
2. Select "None" and close "Properties".

Please continue enjoying game dev life with PGM MV!

notes.title: Submissions for the RPG Maker Horror Festiva are now open!
notes.content:
We are planning a creator-focused horror event, called the RPG Maker Horror Festival, that is open to all Steam games that fall within the horror genre!

Submissions for the event are now open! Other than the basic requirements listed below, the event is open to all games!
And of course we’re hoping many submissions will be looking to use Steam’s Broadcast function too!
If this sounds like the kind of event for your game, please complete the submission form linked below.

notes.title: Release of the Player Component as Open Source
notes.content:
Everyone,
Thank you for your use of Pixel Game Maker MV over the last several years!

After much discussion, we have decided to release the Player component of Pixel Game Maker MV as open source software via a GitHub repository.

At this time, only the Player component, which is used to play games built with Pixel Game Maker MV, will be open sourced. The Editor component will remain closed source for the foreseeable future.

It is our hope to achieve the following 2 objectives with this decision:

[h2]1. Enable creators to use a customized version of the player that improves performance for their game.[/h2]
By writing game-specific code or removing unused functionality, the player component can be customized to be more efficient for a specific game.
Note that due to some security concerns, games built with encrypted data will not load correctly on a customized Player component. We apologize for this limitation, and ask for your understanding.

[h2]2. Improving Bug Fix Rate[/h2]
As the Player will now be open source, it will be possible for anyone in the Pixel Game Maker MV community to submit a pull request for any bugs they find & fix. Contributors will have their names added to the Pixel Game Maker MV developer credits

Please access the Pixel Game Maker MV GitHub repository for details.

We have started the next phase of this project, but we remain committed to Pixel Game Maker MV's continued development. We look forward to improving the experience with you, our community.

[h2]GitHub Repository[/h2]
https://github.com/GGGweb-adm/PGMMV

[h2]Using A Customized Player Component[/h2]
From November 21, 2023, it will be possible to use a customized Player component via the “1.0.6-Osplayer-beta” branch on Steam.
*This is otherwise identical to version 1.0.6.8.

After enabling this branch, you will have the option to specify versions to use for the Player, Runtine, and Debugging Runtime components.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/f76468226a1b79f46093ae5e70ccd12436523805.png[/img]
Player: This is the version of the Player component used when performing a test play via the PGMMV editor.
The default version is the normal Player component installed with PGMMV’s editor at (install folder)/player-win/player.exe.

Runtime: This is the version of the Player component packaged with a game during the build process, and thus is the version people who play your game will use.
The default version is the one included with a PGMMV install: (install folder)/resource/runtime.zip

Debugging Runtime: A version of the Runtime used when a game is built with the debug flag enabled.
The default version is the one included with a PGMMV install: (install folder)/resource/debugMenuRuntime.zip

Currently no components are selected when this beta branch is enabled, so please be sure to select Player components when first using this new branch.

[How to Change Branches]
[h3]Caution: We strongly recommend backing up your project before attempting the following. [/h3]
1.Go to Steam Library, right click "Pixel Game Maker MV" and select "Properties".
2.Click on the "Beta" tab, select the correct version and close "Properties".

[Reverting Back to Default]
Follow the instructions below to switch from the Beta version back to the previous version.
1.Go to Steam Library, right click "Pixel Game Maker MV" and select "Properties".
2.Select "None" and close "Properties".
Please continue enjoying your game dev life with PGMMV!

notes.title: RPG Maker Festival 2023 Starts Today on Steam!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38018723/d663c8da67c98dff633fc1bd62633d6974f948a1.jpg[/img]

The RPG Maker Festival is an annual Steam Sale Event that saw its first occurring in February 2022. It is dedicated to the RPG Maker series, a non-coding engine series well loved by many indie and hobbyist developers from around the globe. 
Not only will the engines be discounted greatly, the 2023 event will also be joined by over 450 RPG Maker-made game titles created by its enthusiastic and eager fan community, including worldly-acclaimed titles such as The Witch's House MV and LISA: The Painful!

[b]RPG Maker Festival 2023 Steam Event Page
[/b]https://store.steampowered.com/sale/rpgmaker_festival_2023

[b]RPG Maker Festival 2023 Event Duration
[/b]Pacific Standard Time: Feb 13, 2023 10:00 AM to Feb 20, 2023 10:00 AM 
Japan Standard Time: Feb 14, 2023 03:00 AM to Feb 21, 2023 03:00 AM


[b]45% OFF on RPG Maker MZ, and 85% OFF on RPG Maker MV！[/b]
The most current RPG Maker title, RPG Maker MZ, will be discounted up to 45% OFF in the 2023 event - the deepest discount to date.
Meanwhile, RPG Maker MV, will be discounted up to 85％ OFF. 
For users who already own other RPG Maker titles, there will also be special bundles available too.

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/30532/2023_MZ_Festival_SPECIAL/

[b]Release of the 3D Character Converter Tool on Steam![/b]
The 3D Character Converter is a convenient mini-app that can quickly convert humanoid-shaped VRM models into 2D character sprite assets compatible with RPG Maker series. Users can either import custom-made or commercially available VRM models into the converter for conversion. The app can output a total of 5 types of map walker sprites, 18 types of side-view battle character (aka SV-Battler) sprites, and the model’s faces for use as character portraits in dialogue boxes common in RPGs. 

Although the 3D Character Converter app was originally designed for the currently in development RPG Maker Unite, there are also options that would allow the converter to output 2D assets compatible with RPG Maker MV and RPG Maker MZ. The developers hope that the early release of this app can provide RPG Maker users a different means of creating game assets for their games.

(What is VRM: A platform-independent file format designed for use with 3D characters and avatars in the VR era. (Please refer to the [url=https://vrm-consortium.org/en/]VRM Consortium[/url] for detail))

[b]RPG Maker 3D Character Converter Product Spec
[/b]※Steam Account and Steam client app required.

■MSRP：$9.99（incl. tax）
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2218350/

（Users can also import VRM models using most VRM generation apps）

[b]PiXel ScaLer Coming to Steam for Free too![/b]
[i]PiXel ScaLer[/i] is a simple but powerful tool that can enlarge and convert pixel arts into higher resolution illustrations. Already released on RPG Maker Unite’s official site, it will now also be available for download on Steam for simpler app management. The tool supports many resolutions which makes it suitable to use with RPG Maker MZ and MV, as well as the RPG Maker Unite currently in development.　

※PiXel ScaLer is a product developed by Nononotyaya-san - who has granted Gotcha Gotcha Games the rights to distribute it as an official tool of RPG Maker series.

[b]SV Battler Sprites[/b]: 64 x 64, 320 x 320, 512 x 512, and 194 x 194 (RPG Maker Unite’s default asset spec)

notes.content:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38018723/06bf7ebc96151cdc89cd4b152147cd9809c7d887.png[/img]

notes.title: Recruiting for game titles made by PGMMV to be published onto Nintendo Switch!
notes.content:
Dear PGM users, 

Thank you for your continued support of Pixel Game Maker MV!

[h3]Are you aware that games made by Pixel Game Maker MV can be published onto the Nintendo Switch platform?[/h3]

That’s right! Even if you do not know any programming, you may still be able to become a game creator of the super popular Nintendo Switch console! So far there have been [b]up to 32 PGM-made games released[/b], with more coming soon!
[previewyoutube=LBOre4x3nxM;full][/previewyoutube]

You can find a list of published PGM titles here!
https://rpgmakerofficial.com/act_game/game/?lang=en

Do note however, that to develop for Nintendo Switch using Pixel Game Maker MV, you will need to setup the dedicated developer environment. A publishing contract with Gotcha Gotcha Games is required for this. 

If you are interested in reading up a little about the dedicated environment, you can find it here: 
https://customers.microsoft.com/en-us/story/1386970234134406611-software-advanced-research-gaming-azure-en-japan
Using our specially designed platform, you will not need the developer's version of Switch console for this!
We do not request additional upfront cost required to obtain this developer environment. However, you will need to have a Nintendo Switch console of your own and internet connectivity.

[h3]The hurdles might seem intimidating, but it is worth a shot![/h3]
[h3]At Gotcha Gotcha Games, we are always recruiting all sorts of titles to publish from PGM users.[/h3]
There will be a screening by us first, followed by Nintendo themselves. Other than this, the opportunities are open to any developers, from anywhere!

If you have games in development or already completed, and are interested in selling on the Nintendo Switch, please consider applying under below link!
https://rpgmakerofficial.com/en/application/action_tkool/

notes.title: (Hot Fix) Update 1.05.13 Released

Dear PGM Users！
Thank you for you continued support of PGM.
We have now updated the default branch to 1.0.5.13.

To all users of Pixel Game Maker MV,　

Starting April 1st, 2022, Gotcha Gotcha Games will take on the role of publisher of Pixel Game Maker MV, succeeding current publisher PLAYISM due to unforeseen circumstances. Following this publisher change on April 1st, Gotcha Gotcha Games will be taking over for PLAYISM for all customer inquiries and technical support. There will be no particular impact to discussion boards such as the Steam Community.

notes.title: Summer Game Jam 2021 - Results!
notes.content:
Hi All!

Today we are very excited to introduce the Top 3 games of Pixel Game Maker MV Summer Game Jam 2021!

This three-week Game Jam has provided many great games, and we are sincerely grateful to everyone in the community for using our software!

[url=https://theramz.itch.io/star][i]Star Surfer[/i] by RamZ[/url]
This game was super enjoyable! You play as an astronaut traversing an unknown planet that happens to have several outhouses scattered around (possible signs of life?). The platform-based puzzles are cleverly designed, and player physics make you feel like you're really in space. In the end you discover that you are not only not alone on the planet, you are about to become something's dinner.
Congrats to RamZ on First Place!
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/baaabda1ec178258701318a4a021144a70d07a80.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/baaabda1ec178258701318a4a021144a70d07a80.gif[/img][/url]

[url=https://lavadropeu.itch.io/oh-starry-knight][i]Oh Starry Knight![/i] by LavadropEU[/url]
You take on the role of Starry Knight, a star that took it upon itself to defend the universe against human invaders. The pixel art was incredible and every second of the game was full of color! The puzzle mechanics added a unique strategic aspect to the gameplay as well.
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/29fba06ac49e6572ebfa3497adf5b21a49280493.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/29fba06ac49e6572ebfa3497adf5b21a49280493.gif[/img][/url]

[url=https://baccaritch.itch.io/vincents-starry-night-sky][i]Vincent's Starry Night Sky[/i] by baccaritch[/url]
Follow the story of Vincent van Gogh in this thought-provoking game. You play as Vincent and travel through his life, painting and gaining a deeper awareness about the struggles of depression. The gameplay changes slightly halfway through, which has Vincent fending for his life against ghostlike beings.
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/00e2cea845100611d820318b35a8cf7902fa41b3.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/00e2cea845100611d820318b35a8cf7902fa41b3.gif[/img][/url]

As a bonus, one of our team members, Baz, and pixel artist Noobk also participated in the Game Jam and ended up with an apocalyptic base defender game,[url=https://bazratcreates.itch.io/starfall-apocalypse] [i]Starfall Apocalypse[/i][/url]. Can you survive the starfall apocalypse for five whole minutes?
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/eb8426aab00fa6d5833c4e11e3179e3d24c9bb53.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/eb8426aab00fa6d5833c4e11e3179e3d24c9bb53.gif[/img][/url]

We would also like to congratulate all of the participants of the Game Jam - the games were awesome and we enjoyed playing every one of them! If you haven't already, please take a look at the [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-summer-game-jam-2021/entries]Submission Page[/url] to download and play!

Hi everyone!

PGMMV's Summer Jam is back! We are very excited to announce our third Game Jam on itch.io!

PGMMV - Summer Game Jam 2021 is a a-little-bit-more-than-2 weeks-long Jam for users of Pixel Game Maker MV hosted by PLAYISM/Active Gaming Media Inc.
The jam runs from [b]August 6th, 10AM JST to August 25th, 10AM JST.[/b]
The theme will be announced on the first day of the Game Jam on the[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-summer-game-jam-2021] itch.io Jam page[/url] and on our [url=https://twitter.com/PixelGameMaker]Twitter account[/url]!

Voting closes and results will be announced on September 6th 10 AM JST. 
The winning titles will be showcased on our Steam page in the following weeks.

Rules:
- Make a game using PGMMV related to the theme!
- You must accept the terms of use of itch.io (https://itch.io/docs/legal/terms)
- Work in team or alone, it is up to you! 
You can use the Community board to find teams."
- You must create and work on the game during the dates specified for this contest.
- You can use pre-existing assets for the Jam, and any assets you have the legal right to use. However, the game project must have been created specifically for the contest.
- The games will be evaluated by the public! Criteria are the respect for the theme, graphics and the gameplay!
The details of the Jam's terms and conditions can be [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-summer-game-jam-2021/topic/1563595/pixel-game-maker-mv-jam-terms-and-conditions-]found here [/url](Japanese and English Only).

How to submit a game:
Click on Join Jam, then Submit your project.
Fill in the application page and upload the file. 
Please set the page to “Public”. 
Be sure to put the game as Free - No paid games will be evaluated.
Please upload a build. Project data won't be evaluated

Important points:
Only games made with the game engine Pixel Game Maker MV will be accepted, but don't worry if you don't own the software: a free demo is available [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/837510/Pixel_Game_Maker_MV/]here[/url]! 

Note that with the demo you cannot build the game, so you can send us your project file to maker_support@activegamingmedia.com and we will send you back a build project. Please kindly note that this service will be offered until August 22th, 5pm JST.

The winning games will be showcased in a post under the "News" tab on Pixel Game Maker MV's Steam page in English, Japanese and Simplified Chinese! 
Thanks to Gotcha Gotcha Games, the 3 best rated games will also receive a set of 3 keys for the following games:

notes.title: Pixel Game Maker MV Game Development Challenge 2020 Winner Announcement
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

You may have watched it live during Indie Live Expo: [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-game-development-challenge-2020/rate/937354]Elfin Force by TacoBee[/url] has won the PGMMV Game Development Challenge 2020! Congratulations!

Here is the ranking and some comments about the games from our judges that we're very excited to share with you.
Full comments will be sent to the participants individually.

[b]4th Ex Aequo[/b]
[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-game-development-challenge-2020/rate/891928]Pentacore Beta Demo by Mythril Age[/url]
Here is a message from Richard Lems:  "A metroid inspired game! I love metroidvanias so I was excited to get started. The game begins with a great little introduction. It really draws the player in. The graphics are minimal but look pretty good, everything is nice and consistent. Presentation wise, this game is really doing a great job!"
and another from Daisuke "Pixel" Amaya: "While simple, progressing through wide maps with the auto-mapping function and non-repelling wall kicks was enjoyable. I also liked the system where you recover energy by evading or beating enemies depending on how much remaining energy you have"

[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-game-development-challenge-2020/rate/935227]GemVenture [DEMO] by JetGames[/url]
Daisuke "Pixel" Amaya has some comments and advice "I really enjoy the spin attack, it is a lot of fun. 
At this stage, the gems scattered throughout the stage does not seem to have any effect.
In the many additional stages to be added, the game definitely needs to give players an incentive to collect the gems. I found this game familiar, then I realized it was the same creator who made Canyon Climb. "
...and so does Takumi Naramura ! '"A simple but difficult jump action game that is flawlessly made. However, there seems to be no other progression method other than the one shown. Before anything else, I would recommend switching the current BGM with one that is more uplifting."

[b]3rd Place[/b]
[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-game-development-challenge-2020/rate/938009]TOWER project DEMO by airbox[/url]
Richard Lems is very enthousiastic about the game's combat "Building up momentum in combat makes you feel like a true badass and I loved that." and wants to see more. "Once I got to town things became more interesting and the game shows a lot of potential for the future.
Daisuke "Pixel" Amaya agrees "I enjoyed how the sword-swinging and magic motions changed depending on the directional keys.
It is well-balanced and the fact that mid-air braking isn't effective makes me want to master it even more.
Graphics, music, and sound effects are all excellent and very well made.
I also like how allies throw you recovery items during battle, which doesn't make the game overly difficult"
Takumi Naramura comes with somemore advice for the creator "The main actions are all implemented in the game but perfecting the difficulty curve (i.e. stage construction), should take priority. "

[b]2nd Place[/b]
[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-game-development-challenge-2020/rate/891341]Eadus Ending by beenbaba[/url]
This entry was actually Richard Lems's big favorite "After logging in to Eadus Online, I’m greeted by lovely characters and a beautiful world. I really like where this is going! Quickly poking around the menus, it seems not everything is working yet, but a lot of it is. Great potential and a real surprise to see something so advanced made with the software. "
Daisuke "Pixel" Amaya is also very curious to see more "It was nice to have different attacking options at the beginning but I found using regular attacks only to be the most fun.
The monsters are cute and I also liked the music.
Considering this is still version 0.11, there should be a lot more to come. Personally, I am curious as to what the game has in store for the characters."
Takumi Naramura stills comes with constructive comments "The screen reminds me of Mega Man Battle Network, but unfortunately I have never played it before so I found it hard to understand the rules. All functions are unlocked, which may be the case because the game is still in development. To avoid confusing players, functions should be unlocked gradually, giving players more functions slowly so they can learn the advantages and disadvantages of each function."

[b]Winner[/b]
[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-game-development-challenge-2020/rate/937354]Elfin Force by TacoBee[/url]
Richard Lems's comment: "Starting up the game I was immediately impressed with the presentation. The UI animations are polished and slick and the title screen was just beautiful. So I was hyped from the start and was eager to get playing.
The shooter gameplay was solid, with a fun twist in that you can reverse your secondary weapon direction. In games like these, I tend to hug the bottom of the screen so I have maximum reaction time. But for this game I had to rethink that strategy and was forced to train my reflexes for dodging.
Overall I had a great time, the transitions in gameplay phases were also executed very well with warnings in the UI etc. The soundtrack was also very fitting and got me in the right mood for playing.  "

Daisuke "Pixel" Amaya is hyped by the graphics :"All visuals from the splash screen to the game's opening are very well-polished, complementing the cool title screen music, prompt introductions, controls, and the characters.I also like having the ability to skip at various points of the game as it makes repeated playthroughs smooth. "

Takumi Naramura was impressed too: "A very well-made throwback of the old arcade shooting games. I'm sure it took a lot of effort and time to implement all the ideas and effects present in the game."

Again and again, thank you to all the participants, we're grateful for your time and your efforts. Please keep working on your games and don't give up!

Check out all the submissions [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-game-development-challenge-2020/entries]here[/url].

notes.content:
Hi all,
We announced it last week, and now the Database Beta Update is finally here!
We have released an update for the branch "1.0.5-database"

If you wish to use the latest Database Beta Version update, please select “1.0.5-database” from the Beta tab.
We strongly recommend you to back-up your projects before proceeding to the update.
The default branch remains branch 1.0.4.

But that is not all! 
As we understand that the Database Function can be a bit hard to use at first, our power-users [url=https://twitter.com/Joewithoutme]Joe[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/BazratCreates]Baz[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/JustusPan]Justus[/url] have prepared some help for you!
The update includes a new sample project featuring two mechanisms, one showing a puzzle mechanism and one showing a level-up system.

Baz and Justus have recorded videos to explain the Database, and you can find them here:
[url=https://youtu.be/Rx_Dfex-fyo ]Baz tutorial[/url] (English with Japanese subtitles)  
[url=https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1mv41147y8/]Justus tutorial [/url](Simplified Chinese) (The tutorial will be released in a few hours)

With the release of the Database, we have achieved a milestone that will allow you to make deeper, more complex games. It is very exciting to see how you will use it!
However, please keep it mind it is still in Beta at this time and we are working hard on the final version. 
In the final version of the database, we plan to facilitate the creation of plugins.
And as usual, if you have any questions, you can find us on the Steam Forums, the support mail address and Twitter!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/673602e5e832d918129f38deae1c5721273b0e25.gif[/img]

[url=https://twitter.com/Dot_Zo_Games]DotZo[/url] has made this project on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/videos/819303097]Twitch[/url] (Japanese only) during the Digital Game Expo 2020, as a collaboration with Sprite Studio.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/ff994d4da540102b88bedd2b6b4f913021613073.gif[/img]

Finally, as the year ends, we would like to wholeheartedly thank you for your support in 2020. 
Everywhere in the world, 2020 has been a tough year, but we are so proud of what the PGMMV community has achieved!
Some of you have released a game, signed with publishers, made tutorials, guides, videos, helped others, participated in Jams and Contests using the engine, given feedback and suggestions... it was a year full of learning and full of surprises!

Our Customer Support team will take a break from December 28th, 2020 to January 4th, 2021 and we will be back next year to assist you!
Sorry in advance for the inconvenience, but please be sure that we can't wait to hear your feedback about the Database Beta version!

Happy Holidays!

Thanks for using Pixel Game Maker MV!

Today we are releasing a DLC pack for Pixel Game Maker MV: the ""Weapon Assets (100 varieties) and Dot Robot Set""!
These were previously only distributed together with the packaged version of Pixel Game Maker MV in Japan, but are now available as DLC!


The "Weapon Assets (100 varieties)" set is chock full of various weapon assets, such as swords, axes, and other melee weapons, as well as staves, bows, and more. notes.title: Pixel Game Maker MV - Anniversary Game Jam 2020
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

As PGMMV celebrates its first anniversary since full release, we are very excited to announce our second Game Jam on itch.io!
[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-anniversary-game-jam-2020]PGMMV - Anniversary Game Jam 2020[/url] is a 2 weeks-long Jam for users of Pixel Game Maker MV hosted by Playism/Active Gaming Media Inc.
The jam runs from September 18th, 10AM JST to October 2nd, 10AM JST.
The theme will be announced on September 18th, 10AM JST (September 17th, 6PM PST) on the[url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-anniversary-game-jam-2020] itch.io Jam page[/url] and on our [url=https://twitter.com/PixelGameMaker]Twitter [/url]account!
Voting closes and results will be announced on October 9th 6PM JST. The winning titles will be showcased on our Steam page the following week.

[b]Rules:[/b]
- Get inspired by the theme and make a game using PGMMV related to it!
- You must accept the terms of use of itch.io [url=https://itch.io/docs/legal/terms](https://itch.io/docs/legal/terms)[/url]
"- Work in team or alone, it is up to you! 
You can use the Community board to find teams."
- You must create and work on the game during the dates specified for this contest.
ｰ You can use pre-existing assets for the Jam, and any assets you have the legal right to use. However, the game project must have been created specifically for the contest.
- The games will be evaluated by the public! Criteria are the respect of the theme and the gameplay!
The details of the Jam's terms and conditions can be found [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-anniversary-game-jam-2020/topic/974942/pixel-game-maker-mv-anniversary-game-jam-2020-terms-and-conditions]here[/url] (Japanese and English Only).

[b]How to submit a game:[/b]
Click on Join Jam, then Submit your project.
Fill in the application page and upload the file. 
Please set the page to “Public”. 
Be sure to put the game as Free - No paid games will be evaluated.
Please upload a build.
Project data won't be evaluated

[b]Important points:[/b]
Only games made with the game engine Pixel Game Maker MV will be accepted, but don't worry if you don't own the software: a free demo is available [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/837510/]here[/url]! 

Note that with the demo you cannot build the game, so you can send us your project file to maker_support@activegamingmedia.com and we will send you back a build project. Please kindly note that this service will be offered until October 1st, 5pm JST.

The winning games will be showcased on our Steam page in English, Japanese and Simplified Chinese! 
If you have questions, please ask directly on the community board or to maker_support@activegamingmedia.com!

Good luck everyone!

notes.title: Pixel Game Maker MV - Summer Game Jam 2020 Winner Announcement!
notes.content:
Hi All!

We are very excited to introduce to you today not only one but the top 3 games of the [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-summer-game-jam-2020]Pixel Game Maker MV - Summer Game Jam 2020[/url]!

This 2 weeks Jam has brought a lot of great games and we are sincerely grateful to the community for using our software!

[h1][url=https://kaizen-nero.itch.io/summer-fun]Summer fun[/url][/h1]
This mini game has swimming mechanics, cool music, and excellent pixel art! The game starts with a couple simple puzzle to solve which leads you to a giant ocean to explore. The way the game went from small to vast exploration was very clever and we really liked the spinning swim attack! 
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/6de6c847256c0e048c47c30e5c87ecc697e7eaaf.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/6de6c847256c0e048c47c30e5c87ecc697e7eaaf.gif[/img][/url][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/b18bbc4187a789bf1a1c28e4b93bcbcb1ba14d3b.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/b18bbc4187a789bf1a1c28e4b93bcbcb1ba14d3b.gif[/img][/url]

[h1][url=https://narehop.itch.io/clamknight]ClamKnight[/url][/h1]
Wow, Narehop does it again with another masterpiece! You play as a young clam named Marvin who has to pass through 17 puzzle levels to become a legendary ClamKnight. The game even comes with a retro style manual to view! Simply a must play and we hope to see more!
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/c210967b2029b376f905705dfa1471fb5d600ae5.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32941247/c210967b2029b376f905705dfa1471fb5d600ae5.gif[/img][/url]

notes.title: Summer Game Jam 2020
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

We are very excited to announce our first Game Jam on itch.io! 
Why not participate while waiting for the results of the Game Development Challenge?

PGMMV - Summer Game Jam 2020 is a 2 weeks-long Jam for users of Pixel Game Maker MV hosted by [url=http://publishing.playism-games.com/]Playism[/url]/[url=https://activegamingmedia.com/en/]Active Gaming Media Inc.[/url]
The jam runs from June 26th, 10AM JST to July 10th, 10AM JST.

 The theme will be announced on June 26th, 10AM JST (June 25th, 6PM PST) on the [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-summer-game-jam-2020]itch.io Jam page [/url]and on our [url=https://twitter.com/PixelGameMaker]Twitter account![/url]


This time, the rules are pretty straightforward:
- Get inspired by the theme and make a game using PGMMV related to it!
- Anyone aged 16 or older can enter.
- Work in team or alone, it is up to you! You can use the Community board to find teams.
- You must create and work on the game during the dates specified for this contest.
ｰ You can use pre-existing assets for the Jam, and any assets you have the legal right to use. However, the game project must have been created specifically for the contest.
The details of the Jam's terms and conditions can be found here.

Only games made with the game engine Pixel Game Maker MV will be accepted, but don't worry if you don't own the software: a free demo is available [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/837510/Pixel_Game_Maker_MV/]here[/url]! 

Note that with the demo you cannot build the game, so you can send us your project file to maker_support@activegamingmedia.com and we will send you back a build project. Please kindly note that this service will be offered until July 9th, 5pm JST


The games will be evaluated by the public! 
Criteria are the respect of the theme and the gameplay.

The winning game will be showcased on our Steam page in English, Japanese and Simplified Chinese! 

If you have questions, please ask directly on the itch.io [url=https://itch.io/jam/pixel-game-maker-mv-summer-game-jam-2020/community]community board [/url]or by email to maker_support@activegamingmedia.com !

notes.title: Pixel Game Maker MV - New Roadmap Announcement!
notes.content:
Hi all,

Thanks for supporting Pixel Game Maker MV.

We have listened closely to everyone's requests, and now we would like to share with you the newly-revamped roadmap for the future of Pixel Game Maker MV.
Put simply, we will develop and roll out the upcoming features and functions in the following order:
[olist]
[*]  Addition of Database functionality
[*]  Addition of settings for erasing Attack detection in motion settings when an object hits Collision detection while Attack detection is valid
[*]  Addition of ability to copy shortcut nodes and action boxes
[*]  Addition of slider to adjust Object RGB
[*]  Addition of ability to acquire analog stick angle and inclination
[*]  Addition of string variables and input runtime actions  [list]
[*] Action text display, scrolling text display also supported
[*] Tag embedding support
[*] Both keyboard and digital keyboard input supported[/list]
[*]  Addition of function for adding and deleting options to the game player pulldown menu
[*]  Roguelike features
[/olist]

The long-awaited database function will be finished up and rolled out first!

We will continue to put our all into development on our end, so in the meantime we hope you all continue to enjoy creating the games of your dreams using Pixel Game Maker MV!

notes.title: Version 1.0.4.0 Update
notes.content:
Hi All,

Thank you very much for using Pixel Game Maker MV.
Version 1.0.4.0 has just been released.


This time, the update has been uploaded to the "1.0.4" branch as a beta version. 
If you wish to use 1.0.4.0 update, please select “1.0.4” from the Beta tab.

Version 1.0.4.0 Update
[h1]Additions[/h1][list]
[*]Added a setting to slopes placed in scene so as Objects stop being ”stuck” to them
[*]Added a setting to maintain or increase the magnification ratio when changing the window size or full screen
[*]Added a function to change the Animation Set 
[list][*]Added the functionality to add Animation Sets in the Animation Settings
The added Animations will feature the same number of divisions as the main Animation
[*]Added the functionality to change and preview the Animation Set in the Animation timeline preview
[*]Added the Runtime Action "Change Animation Set"[/list]
[*]Added the functionality to set the origin and connection point as the destination of the Object in the Runtime Action" Move Object"
[*]Updated the help documentation for Plugin
[*]Added "Blink" to the Object's Filter Effects
[*]The area to input text and scripts can now be reduced or enlarged
[*]The Scroll Speed for each layer in the Scene Settings can now be set separately for the X and Y directions.
[*]In build where encryption is enabled, Save Data created is also Encrypted. Please note the following points in game that execute Save Load:
[list][*]Be sure to set an encryption key when building the game
[*]Use the same encrypted key when updating the game to a newer version
If no key or a wrong key is set, the compatibility of the save files will be lost [/list]
[*]Added a plug[*]in that adjusts the volume of the SE based on the distance to the object to the official plugins.
[/list]
[h1]Bug Fixes (Player)[/h1][list]
[*]Fixed the "sticky slope" issue
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Wall Detection to not work as intended when there are several Wall Detection 
[*]Fixed a bug that caused trouble in the display of loops when setting an image as the background of a scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a discrepancy in the display of the Display Direction when moving the Object back and forth and turning
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the "Move Towards Display Direction" to not applied even if the Display Direction Variable was changed.
[*]Fixed a bug where the player could get stuck on a tile when jumping
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when test playing a project without a Start Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Scripts to not be executable in Common Actions
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Script set for an Object to be executed even if  "Execute Script" was changed after being placed in the scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Scripts to not be executed after the Object disappeared
[*]Fixed a bug that caused multiple Player Objects to be displayed when moving through a portal
[*]Fixed a bug that caused to not proceed the Condition Links and Actions of one frame when generating scenes
[*]Fixed a bug that caused set duration to remain the same even after changing the "Duration to take over accelerated speed"
[*]Fixed a bug that caused "Change Game Speed" to be disabled on Set Object Single/All
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the sound of Videos to be included in BGM volume in Sound Settings
[*]Fixed a bug that caused input to be detected when the input reception frame was 1 or more and the game speed at 0%
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a crash when the invincibility was set to 1 second or less and a Filter Effect was applied
[*]Fixed a bug that caused sound to be not played when resetting with F
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Variables not to be updated when a Locked Object moved to another layer
[*]Fixed a bug that caused troubles in Child object to follow the Parent Object when the movement was small
[*]Fixed a bug that caused operation of an Object to stop when "Wait" was executed
[*]Fixed a bug that caused "Attach Generated Object to Grid" not to work as intended
[*]Fixed a bug that caused "Coordinates are Display Area-based" in "Move Object" not to work as intended
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a crash when Object had no motion set and "Stop Object Animations During Move" was enabled
[*]Fixed a bug that enabled Gimmick Tile in set Layer even if the Layer is disabled
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the display priority of generated Objects to not be saved
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Object group added on "Attack Settings" to not be saved when loading a file
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a crash when switching the motion of an object to one with no display direction
[*]Fixed a bug that caused "Change Object" not to work as intended when using a Connection point
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the debug settings to reset after building a game
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the afterimage of an inherited motion not to work as expected
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Link Condition "Specified Object's Action Changes"'s action list not to update
[*]Fixed a bug that caused mouse's wheel up / down scrolling was not detected as input
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Objects transferred through a Portal to be displayed behind the tiles when using Screen Effects
[*]Fixed a bug that caused "Other After Destruction Settings" to be not executed after "Destroy Object"
[*]Fixed a bug that caused "Disable Screen Shake" to be canceled when updating the Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a discrepancy in the position of Physics Objects when loading a file
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Objects with "Fix Relative Position to Camera" to disappear when saving and loading
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a crash when the direction of "Set Move Direction and Move" was erased
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the instance id to change when "Reset Switch/Variable" was executed
[*]Fixed a bug that caused invincibility effects to disappear when switching animation
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Filter Effects to be reinitialized if the Animation Resource was different for each Action
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Common Actions to not be detected in the transition from the initial action when generating a scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused an offset in the coordinates of an object when the specified object of a Runtime Action was on a different layer with a different scrolling speed
[*]Fixed a bug that caused an offset in coordinates at the time of generations when the Camera Tracking in on a layer with a scroll speed of 0%
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when " Not set" was selected as a connection point for "Push/Pull Object" 
[*]Fixed a bug that caused problems in the generation of a Child Object's Child when saving and loading
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the order in which Objects were generated by connection to be changed when transitioning between Scenes
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a crash when there is no Display Direction of the Animation when displaying the afterimage
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the state at the end of a scene to be discarded by save and load when an Object has "Maintain State at End of Scene" enabled at positioned in a menu scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a crash when displaying a text with tags in Object display and Parent-Child text display
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the game to stop progressing when loading a file
[/list]
[h1]Adjustment (Player)[/h1][list]
[*]Fixed the effects of Damage taking over
[*]Changed "Maintain State at End of Scene" so that it is also enabled on Menu Scenes
[*]Changed Particle display when set behind a Connection Point
[*]Reduced the processing when drawing scene during game play
[*]Fixed a phenomenon that caused objects to get easily buried in Gimmick Tiles
[/list]
[h1]Bug Fixes (Editor)[/h1][list]
[*]Suppressed "Object Self" from the below Condition Settings
[list][*]Contact with Wall Detection of Other Objects
[*]Discovered Other Object
[*]Other Objects Facing Specified Direction[/list]
[*]Added the setting "Object Other Than Self" to the below Other Runtime Actions
[list][*]Move Object
[*]Push/Pull Object[/list]
[*]Fixed the display of custom keys on bright theme
[*]Lightened copy/paste processing of Tiles in the scene layout
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a crash when the value of a tile was updated 
[*]Fixed a bug that caused decimals to be set in the Bullet Settings's "Shoot in Fixed Direction" and "Expand Firing Range:"
[*]Fixed a bug that caused "Right" to be displayed instead of an arrow
[*]Added a scroll bar to the following text display area:
[list][*]Plugin action description
[*]"Content:" when displayed at the time of an Import or an Export [/list]
[*] Fixed the problem that caused scrolling up and down with the mouse wheel to not function properly when the mouse cursor is over "Check motion" in the Action Settings
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the layer list to not work in the list of Layout in the Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a slow[*]down when "Lock Object" was set to "Runtime Action Changeable Even After Placement"
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Setting Screen to not update when selecting the Link or Action with the keyboard.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused AND and OR to disappear when Other Conditions were moved by dragging
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a custom resolution to be applied even when selecting another resolution 
[*]Adjusted the processing of Scenes with a high number of Tiles
[/list]


How to switch to Branches
1. Open "Properties" for Pixel Game Maker MV in your Steam Library.
2. Select the Beta tab and select the target version and close Properties.

How to switch to Default
Please execute the following process to revert from other versions to the current release.
1. Open "Properties" for Pixel Game Maker MV in your Steam Library.
2. Select "None - don't participate in any Beta programs" and close Properties.

In addition, at the time of this update, branches of the versions before full release have been deleted.
Please contact our customer support (maker_support@activegamingmedia.com) if you have any problems.

notes.title: Version 1.0.3.0 Update
notes.content:
"Hi All,

Thank you very much for using Pixel Game Maker MV.
Version 1.0.3.0 has just been released."
[h1]Additions[/h1][list]
[*]Added "Release Lock" to Runtime Action 
[*]Added function that when new text is added by "Show Scrolling Text" and "Show Text" is named after the first 10 characters entered when added to Text resources
[*]Added the functionality to adjust anti-aliasing of TTF fonts
[*]Added the possibility to change the background color of Menu Scene (*Not reflected in-game)
[*]Added Transparency to  "Apply Filter Effects On Object"
[*]Added the display of Variable and Switch's memo on-cursor 
[*]Adjusted the behavior of the Child Object "Keep track of the parent object at regular interval", added a "Tracking Accuracy" setting
[*]Added adjustment items related to Wall Detection in the Project Settings
[*]Added the option ”Disable Screen Shake” to the Game's menu
[list][*]The Runtime action "Shake Scene" is disabled[/list]
[*]Added a plug-in to get the Language selected during the game
[/list]
[h1]Bug Fixes (Player)[/h1][list]
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the variable " Display Direction" to not be updated
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a difference in the display of Physics Objects between the Editor and the Player
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when an object is created without motion settings
[*]Fixed a bug that caused objects with the setting "Not Pushed Back by Other Objects" to have unexpected behavior when on a slope
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when the loop set on a music is too short
[*]Fixed the behavior of "Set Duration Until Target Position (Seconds)" if using "Use Basic Move Parameter of Target Object" in "Move Object"
[list][*]Even when "Set Duration Until Target Position (Seconds)" is set, the movement can be changed by a jump or a directional move[/list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused deleted text to be late by 1F
[*]Fixed a bug that caused actions like "Fire Bullet" and "Generate Object" to function, even when the action is switched, if the animation is the same before the transfer
[*]Fixed a bug that caused bitmap to be used when setting a specific size of TTF
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the display direction to reset by the Runtime Action "Move Towards Display Direction"
[*]Fixed a bug that caused gauges to not be displayed as intended
[*]Fixed a bug that caused controller ID to be reset even when changed to "-1"
[*]Fixed a bug in the behavior of manipulated objects when they push each other 
[*]Changed the condition "Change Switch, Variable" to "When a player who has not touched the portal touches" in the Portal Condition Settings "Setting When Touched by Player" 
[*]Fixed a bug that caused characters controlled by keyboard to be controlled by both keyboard and controllers
[*]Fixed a bug in the Invincibility Related Settings
[list][*]If Invincibility Switch was not set, the object was constantly invincible
[*]The Invincibility Related Settings will be enabled when the Object's Invincibility Switch is ON or when the Object touches an Attack Detection box[/list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused an increased processing load then "Shake Scene" is executed while displaying a lot of text in the scene
[list][*]Adjusted in addition to the previous version update[/list]
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when a "Move Object" Runtime action is executed for an Object in a Menu Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Wall Detection of Objects in Menu Scene to not be displayed in debug mode  
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the tracking by Child object to not work as expected when the Parent Object changes by "Change Object"  
[*]Fixed a bug that caused some webm files to not be read correctly
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Bullets which are set on tracking to move to the target coordinates at the time of firing
[*]Fixed a bug that caused child objects to be deleted when moving through a portal after loading the file
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the jump to continue to rise after restarting the game, when stopped and displaying text
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the movement of an Object set with the Runtime Action "Move Object" to continue even if the game speed is set to 0%
[/list]
[h1]Adjustment (Player)[/h1][list]
[*]Adjusted the behavior of Scroll and Show All Players and of Increase or Decrease Display to Show all Players
[*]Adjusted so as the priority of the camera is set in the order of players from 1 to 4 and adjusted so as to avoid the camera to move unexpectedly when the other players go out of the camera
[*]Adjusted the Portal Transfer to transfer Child Objects generated by Child Objects too
[*]Adjusted the behavior when the same SE is played simultaneously in a large number
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when moving a layer and referencing an invalid layer
[/list]
[h1]Bug Fixes (Editor)[/h1][list]
[*]Fixed bugs in the sample games
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause thumbnail to not display the frame settings changes in "Display Direction"
[*]Fixed a bug that caused items not to be displayed when quotations marks are used in the names of switch and variables
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the information of the selected item not to be updated after a drag and drop in a list
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when playing a sound
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the object not to display when copy and pasting an action enabling  Runtime Action Changeable Event After Placement in Scene
[list][*]When a project is loaded, if there is a similar detection, it will be corrected automatically[/list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused an object enlarged at the size of the scene to be positioned with a slight offset or moving in a different direction
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the specified layer by an action to shift when layers are added or the order changed in a scene
[/list]

notes.title: Version 1.0.2.0 Update
notes.content:
Hi All,

Thank you very much for using Pixel Game Maker MV.
Version 1.0.2.0 has just been released.

[h1]Additions[/h1][list]
[*]Added tutorial and help in Simplified Chinese
[*]Added a Text Search function
[*]Added new settings to "Load a File" in Other Runtime Actions
[*]Added Background to "Change Scrolling Speed" in the Scene Settings
[list][*]In addition, the background setting "Scroll Speed / Direction" has been changed to "Auto Scroll Speed / Direction"[/list]
[*]Added an "Update" option on the right click menu of Resources to update several resources at the same time
[*]Added the functionality that when the Object Variable "Animation Frame" is "-2", the animation is stopped at the frame currently being played
[list][*]After stopping at "-2", the Variable automatically changes to the value of the frame it is stopped at[/list]
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes (Player)[/h1][list]
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause "Template Move Settings" to not work as expected after an action involving moving
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent Particles from being generated by an Object when moving to another Layer
[*]Fixed a bug that could display the same Object several times just after using a Portal Transfer
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a discrepancy between a Child Object and Parent Object's angle

notes.title: Version 1.0.1.0 Update
notes.content:
Hi All,

Thank you very much for using Pixel Game Maker MV.
Version 0.1.0.1.0 has just been released. 

[h1]Additions[/h1]
[list]
[*]Added the functionality to assign fonts per language in the Fonts tab (Resources)
When an existing project is loaded, all languages are assigned the same font
[*]Added the ability to move an object using coordinates from within the current screen during gameplay via the "Move Object" Runtime Action
[*]Added the “Get Object Coordinates from Game Screen” plugin to the list of official plugins
When a plug-in is installed, an action with the same name is added to “Other Runtime Actions”
[*]Added the capability to copy-paste ”Other Condition Settings” by adding the right-click menu for the Screen Flow function
[*]The scroll position of the Scene Editor screen is now maintained per scene
[*]In Display and parent-child relationship → Received Damage as Child Object → “Parent Object HP Changes”, the actual behavior was different. The revised text is “Change Target Parent Object” 
  [list][*] Added the checkbox ”Apply Damage Rate to Parent" to decrease the damage received by the Child Object [/list]　
[*]Added a Beat 'em up example to the Sample projects
[*]When opening the software, the logo displayed when starting the editor has been updated to provide information about the Pixel Game Maker MV Game Development Challenge. It can be clicked to open the Challenge website
[*]Increased the maximum amount of “Undo” operations possible
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes (Player)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Action Program and Transition Link Condition "Change Switch/Variable" to behave in an unexpected manner when the target "All" is used
 [list][*] The "All" setting will now determine whether any of the targets have had a switch or variable change that satisfies the configured condition  [/list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Objects with a modified animation scale or center to have differing positions between Scene layout and test play
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Link Conditions to not work as expected when the "Data of Common Variables and Switches" debug menu is opened
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Gimmick Tile and Portal switches to respond poorly to touching Objects
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented the Opacity setting from working as expected when using the "Sequence for Overlaps" settings
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the "Generate Object" to not work when performed via the "Object Settings After Destruction" function
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented Objects from climbing Slopes when "Don't Drop Levels" is enabled for "Template Move Settings"
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent the BGM from playing after repeated Save/Load operations
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Physics Objects that had been added by the Physics Calculation Related Settings to be affected by display scale changes
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent Objects from interacting with Physics Objects after changing Layers via Portal
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented the Physics Influence settings for an Object from being changed by a Switch
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Afterimages to not be displayed when the Interval value was too short
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Camera to ignore its initial position when moving the Camera via Course while auto scrolling is enabled for the Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Tiles with an Opacity value of less than 255 to turn white during Transitions
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash or a significant offset when an Object with added Physics Calculation Parts moves to another layer
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Object not changing directions when touching an upper or lower Wall
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented the "Animation frame" Variable from functioning as intended
[*]Fixed a bug that would cause Objects moving with the "Random" parameter for "Template Move Settings" to stop moving after colliding with a Wall
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the F5 reset to restart the game with the incorrect settings
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the "Shoot at the Selected On-Screen Object Group(s)" parameter for "Bullet Settings" to prioritize the newer Objects when several Objects/Groups are selected
 [list][*] The closest Objects will now be targeted  [/list]
[*]Fixed a bug that would cause text display corruption when using the "Shake Scene" Runtime Action
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Tile Groups and Objects that should not touch to be treated as touching
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Bullets to stop spawning after disabling then re-enabling Layer motion in some cases
"[*]Fixed a bug that could result in Objects becoming offset due to an improperly detected animation Origin when the animation's Origin and Center are not the same point or an Offset has been used to adjust the animation
 [list][*]  Any Runtime Actions that rely on parameters such as “Center of This Object” (including “Generate Object” and “Move Object”) are affected by this fix.  [/list]"
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the camera to become offset when an Object moves to another layer
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a Gimmick Tile using the "When Object Overlaps Tile" setting to function even when the Layer it is placed in is disabled
[*] Fixed a problem that caused an Object to be able to be moved if it is riding on top of another Object even when the "Not Pushed Back by Other Objects" setting is enabled
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Bullets to be fired in a group if the Connection Point used to fire those Bullets is only enabled during the animation
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when using Disable Layer Motion while displaying an effect using a Gimmick Tile
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause "Move Toward Display Direction" to function in unexpected ways when a Tile is touched 
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a Scene to crash when an Animation without a Motion is placed in that Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that prevents the Enlarge Display setting to not offer the x5~8 parameters when playing a game
[*]Fixed a bug that prevents Objects from changing Actions until the "Move Object" action is completed, even if a valid Link Condition allows Action change
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent an Object from being pushed if it is moving fast/has a lot of inertia
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause small Offset values from not displaying correctly during testplay when using              Interpolation
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the "Bound" parameter for "Template Move Settings" to not work when the Object hits a wall
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent Overlap settings from being rendered properly if a partially transparent Tile is placed in a foreground Layer
[*]Fixed a bug that caused SpriteStudio data to behave differently when previewed and during gameplay
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Afterimages to not work as expected after increasing the game's speed
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Gimmick Tile "When Tile's Attack Detection is Touched" setting from not working when attacks are received from certain directions
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Parent Object's Offset to be ignored when a Child Object is following the Parent Object
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause pixel information to be lost in some cases when a Scene Layer's Scroll Speed is not at 100%
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Object Effects to remain visible even if the Scene changes or is otherwise hidden
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Objects to always be displayed in the foreground when using a Portal
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent a Tile from being detected as a part of the correct Tile Group if that Tile was changed as a result of using the "Change tile" function for Gimmick Tiles
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented Bullets from being generated with the correct orientation for Objects using animations created using the "Rotate and Auto-generate" setting
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Objects moved with "Move Object" to have an incorrect Origin point
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when the "Data of Common Variables and Switches" debug menu is opened
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when opening the Operation settings (keymap) for built games
 [*]Fixed a bug that caused the Objects generated by Gimmick Tiles to behave in an unexpected manner
[/list]

[h1]Adjustments (Player) [/h1]
[list]
[*]Adjusted movement handling for Objects to reduce the chances of getting caught on a Slope
[*]Revised Portal movement to prevent duplicating an Action that was being performed when Portal movement was initiated
[*]Changed looping Effects and Particles generated by an Object so that they do not disappear after using a Portal
[*]Revised behavior of the "Stick to Parent Object" setting to reduce occurences of collision detection issues for the Child Object
[*]The Player Detection Object variable is now limited to the values 0~4.
[*]Improved performance of the "Other Runtime Actions" and "Other Condition Settings" window
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes and Changes (Editor)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug that caused a behavorial difference between the layout view and test play when the "Keep Aspect Ratio and Enlarge" is checked for Backgrounds in the Scene Settings
[*]Fixed a bug that caused unusual scroll behavior in some situations when selecting items in a list with Ctrl+click
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent the addition of a Keyframe for Effect Animations 
[*]Fixed some assorted UI issues
[*]Fixed several bugs that could result in a crash
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Tile's Animation Preview to take a longer time than the actual time
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when adding many Tilesets to a Scene
[*]Projects without configured Language Settings will be assigned the OS language when they are next loaded
[*]Fixed a bug that caused an error with the "Load" or "Update" buttons when a Resource is deleted from the Project folder and not from the Editor
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause settings for a different animation to be displayed
[*]Fixed a bug that could prevent large Projects from being opened
[*]Revised the "Show Message" Plug-in to continuously displayed messages without opening/closing the text window when executing multiple Show Message actions within the same Runtime Action
 [list][*]To update an existing project using this plug-in, click the "Update" button on the Plug-in tab and the plug-in will update to the new version [/list]
[/list]

notes.content:
Hello Everyone!

We are proud to announce the release of the v1.0.0 of Pixel Game Maker MV!
We received a lot of constructive feedback during the Early Access, and it helped us to improve the software greatly.

In addition to our coming out of the Early Access period, we are also about to release a 30-day trial version of Pixel Game Maker MV! 

Also, don't forget about the upcoming [b]Pixel Game Maker MV Game Development Challenge![/b]
The contest will start on [b]October 3rd[/b], and the winner will have their submission released on the Nintendo Switch. Any combination of art style and genre are welcome!
For more info, please visit our Itch.io page from October 3rd.
Please give it a try! We are looking forward to seeing your projects!

October 3rd will also see a physical release of Pixel Game Maker MV in Japan, but Steam users shall not be forgotten! To celebrate the launch, Pixel Game Maker is [b]now 30% off![/b]

Finally, 1.0.0 is not the final update for Pixel Game Maker MV!
We spent our time in Early Access focused on building a stable platform, and we feel that we have finally achieved that goal.
Going forward, our focus will be on addressing user requests for quality of life and functional enhancements, such as UI refinements or the addition of functionality like a database system.
Please stay excited for these future updates as we continue onwards!

Thank you for your support of Pixel Game Maker MV!

notes.title: Version 0.9.7.1 Update
notes.content:
Hi All,

Thank you very much for using Pixel Game Maker MV.
Version 0.9.7.1 has just been released. Please check the Steam properties Beta tab to access previous versions.

Additionally, the Player Performance Preview build has also received updates, which are included in the following releases notes.

[h1]■Updates[/h1]

[h1]Additions[/h1]
[list]
[*]Added coordinate information for physics simulation parts to the Scene layout panels
[*]Added x5, x6, x7, and x8 to the Project "Enlarged Display" settings
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes (Default & Preview)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug that let the system know when an Object reached the top of its jump
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause some stickiness when a Slope is placed in front of a Gimmick Tile
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause an Object to get stuck to a wall if an Action Node change occurs with no condition when next to the edge of the valid movement area
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause an Object using Template Move Settings from going up or down a Slope when "Don't Drop Levels" is selected
[*]Fixed a bug that could allow Objects to act even when "Stop All Object Motions" is selected for "Play Video" or "Display Image"
[*]Fixed a bug that would result in Parent-Child relationships not being maintained on Save/Load operations
[*]Fixed a bug that would prevent Objects from updating their display direction when using "Template Move Settings"
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented Object Locking from working as intended when an Object is using a Field of Vision or Lighting setting
[*]Fixed a bug where Child Objects could be scaled to twice the intended size when inheriting Scale from the Parent Object
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Child Objects to rotate too much when using the "Rotate and Auto-generate" animation setting
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented Gimmick Tiles from functioning on using the Overlaps Tile condition
[*]Fixed a bug that would apply anti-alias improperly in some cases when using the "Show Text" Action
[*]Fixed a bug where Gimmick Tils would not properly update in some cases when an Object moving via "Template Move Settings" triggered the tile
[*]Fixed a bug where Objects displayed in the menu were being improperly rotated based on the current Scene
[*]Fixed a bug where Objects assigned to the Player Group would stop following assigned Courses after a Save/Load operation
[*]Fixed a bug where animations could rarely become offset by 1 frame
[*]Fixed a bug where following Child Objects would follow the Parent Object improperly after Scene start
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when moving via Portal when an Object has "Maintain State at End of Scene" enabled
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when previewing particle animations
[*]Fixed a bug that was preventing the "Releasing" Condition from working as intended
[*]Fixed a bug that was causing the "Invincibility" status from lasting longer than specified
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented animations carried over from a Transition from not working after a Save/Load operation
[*]Fixed a bug that made it possible for Objects with multiple wall collision detection areas to get stuck in a wall in certain cases
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented the "Change Camera Display Area" function from working as intended immediately after loading a Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that would cause unintended interactions between Objects on a Course and Slopes
[*]Fixed a bug that would cause a crash if an image-based font has a blank Character Placement field 
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the HP variable to become -1 after adjusting variable values using Course movement, Gimmick Tiles, or Portal movement
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Gimmick Tiles to detect the initial scale values for an Object after changing that Object's scale
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Objects with the "Restore with Action" setting to restore according "Scene Changed" condition
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Gimmick Tiles to be improperly triggered by Objects in other Layers
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Tiles to be improperly colored after changing a Tile's color and then editing a Gimmick Tile
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the Player Object to become unresponsive depending on certain combinations of Gravity strength and direction
[*]Fixed a bug that could improper display of text when text is displayed in certain positions on screen
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause animations that play in reverse from working properly after a Common Action has been used
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause unintended slow movement speeds after a fast moving Object switches to the "Template Move Settings" Action
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes (Player Preview)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug that was causing a memory leak on frequent uses of Portal transitions
[*]Fixed a bug that could result in Object bouncing back from a collision with another Object
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the debug functions to no longer be displayed
[*]Fixed a bug that could allow effect animations to still be played even when the layer 
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause improper display offset when using the Slide (Link) setting for Portals
[*]Fixed a bug that cause adjustments to spawn location for the "Generate Object" Action from taking effect in some cases
[/list]

notes.title: Release of Player Performance Preview Build
notes.content:
Greetings all!

As many you have been requesting for several months, we have been hard at work on a major performance enhancement for Pixel Game Maker MV games.

If you go to the new beta branch, Player Performance Preview, you can try an early test version of this new player component.

This new player should offer much improved performance over the existing player component, whether you are testing your game from the editor component or sharing a built game with a friend.

However, as it is still in a more experimental state, please understand that there could be more bugs in the standard release. We hope that anyone that gives this preview build a try will be sure to share your feedback with us!

[h1]■Updates[/h1]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
 [*] Fixed a bug that caused transparency settings to be applied twice to particles
[/list]

[h1]Changes/Adjustments[/h1]
[list]
[*] Improved performance when no screen effects are in use
 [*] Added 2 new layer selections to the Scenes Effects selection menu
  Compared to other selections, these new selections should have higher performance
  To disable the new "Foremost Layer + Menu" selection, the same setting must be selected
  The new Foremost Layer setting can be disabled via disabling "Foremost Layer" or "All Layers in Scene"
 [*] Changed the name of the Screen Effect setting "All" to "All Layers in Scene". No function changes were made
 [*] Fixed performance when playing the game in an enlarged window
[*] Revised collision detection to now be handled via multi-threaded processing
[/list]
