[*]Fixed a bug where Template Move Settings could be applied by other Runtime Actions
[*]Fixed a bug where afterimages could receive uninteneded effects from changing the game speed 
[*]Fixed a bug where changing the game speed could cause an animation to become desynced
[*]Fixed a bug where an Object using Back and Forth Moving and Turning could be pushed back by other Objects, even when that setting is disabled
[*]Fixed a bug where the Object Switch "Disable" was not working as intended in some cases
[*]Fixed a bug where connected Objects could become improperly offset after a portal transition
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Object coordinates to not be updated if the coordinates were changed in the initial Action 
[*]Fixed a bug that could delete Tiles if a physics was enabled on an Object
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause screen scrolling to be incorrect
[*]Fixed a bug that resulted in some Switches & Variables not being processed properly on Save/Load operations
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Object Wall Detection areas to overlap
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Player movement limitations to be disabled after using Change Camera Display Area
[*]Fixed a bug that could result in Objects not falling if a tile's wall detection is touched at the peak of a jump
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause "Auto-adjust Association Within Specified Dots" to not function in some situations
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause an Object to retain the coordinates of the previous Scene after using a portal to move to a different Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that was preventing the "Contact with a Tile's Wall Detection When Moving One Tile" from working as intended
[*]Fixed a bug that was causing gravity settings to generate discrepancies in how long it took to destroy Objects 
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Objects to move further than intended when using Runtime Action movement commands
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause incorrect controller IDs after using the F5 reset key
[*]Fixed an issue that could cause camera zoom settings to be lost after switching cameras
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the camera and Scene to become offset when the camera display area is equal to the Scene size
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause unintended behavior when an Object fired as a Bullet uses the "Stop" setting from "Template Move Settings"
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when two Objects are connected via a Connection Point and the base Object is destroyed
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause Common Actions to be repeated for no reason in rare circumstances
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause an Object to not update the display direction when a motion is inherited via the "Takes over a motion" setting
*If not wanting to update the display direction on purpose, make use of the "Ignore Direction Change During Motion" setting
[*]Fixed a bug that could result in the Save File, Load File, Delete File, and Copy File Switches not functioning as expected if enabled-disabled quickly  
[*]Fixed a bug that would allow input from unsupported controllers by forcibly assigning a non-existent Controller ID
[*]Fixed a bug that caused text displayed on the menu Scene to be blurry
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause hitching when traversing a reversed Circle Course
[*]Fixed a bug that would cause a crash if a Bullet was fired with only a Connection Point configured in the animation data for that Object
[/list]

[h1]Changes/Adjustments (Player)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Enabled Lighting elements to rotate with the Object they are applied to
[*]Updated behavior of the save file loading and copying operations
[*]Updated Player Group Objects to continue following Template Movement if that movement was interrupted by another non-movement Action
*Movement from an input device will always cancel Template Move settings
[*]Adjusted Attack Settings so that they are updated more frequently 
[*]Reduced performance impact of the official Minimap plug-in
* If already using this plugin in a project, please access the plug-in list and refresh the plug-in to update to the new version
[*]Objects are no longer displayed if the Object they are Connected to has an empty Connection Point keyframe
[*]Revised Bullet settings to prevent Bullets from being fired if the firing Object has an empty Connection Point keyframe
[*]An Object can no longer be spawned if the spawning Object has an empty Connection Point keyframe
[*]Revised the Save File/Load File functions to properly save Object XY scale values
[*]Object relational coordinates are now fixed for Objects spawned via Connection Points
* To make fine adjustments to the display location, please adjust the Connection Point
[*]Revised handling to prevent a possible crash that could occur when loading a save file created with an older version of the project
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes (Editor)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug that could incorrectly introduce decimal numbers when placing an Object in a Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when clicked on UI elements while editing an Object name
[*]Fixed an issue that could cause the background to display improperly after setting the transparency value to 0 and reloading editor
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when repeatedly opening different Projects with various Tile sizes
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the flag icon to be display in the incorrect location after switching scenes and assigning a new Start Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that could sometimes cause a crash when opening a list folder while list icons were being updated
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause an invalid Layer to be displayed in the project after deleting a Layer
[*]Fixed a bug that would cause a crash if a Gimmick Tile was deleted while that tile's Gimmick Settings were actively displayed
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash after switching from the Object tab to the Transitions tab and performing some edits
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause an Object with an enabled transparency setting to be displayed improperly in some sitations
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause invalid data involving coordinates and scaling settings for Objects using an animation that contains empty frame information, when that Object is placed in a Scene
[*]Fixed a bug that could rarely cause a crash after performing Copy/Paste, Undo, and Redo actions when editing an Object's Action Program
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash if a Switch and a Folder shared the same name
[*]Fixed a bug that could rarely cause a crash when opening the Scene Settings dialogue
[*]Fixed the text tag for the Help section regarding Variables
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the "Set Action Display Direction Separately" to be reset after switching tabs
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a crash after changing animation frames while another frame's thumbnail is being generated
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause a numerical spin box to continuously increase if the focus window is changed
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the display direction to become empty for the "Set Move Direction and Move"
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause the points for a Circle Course to become offset
[/list]

[h1]Changes/Adjustments (Editor)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Updated Build path to output to the assigned folder, and allow direct text editing of the path
[*]Adjusted new keyframes for detection areas so that they now spawn at the size of the sprite used for the animation frame
[*]Angles of 15 degrees can now be force selected by holding the Shift key when adjusting angles via the angle selection UI
[*]Objects are now displayed using their configured display directions upon being placed into a Scene
[/list]

[h1]Changes/Adjustments (Sprite Studio)[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue that could result in incorrect coordinates for animations imported from a SSPJ file
[*]Mask and mask strength are now properly supported
[*]Fixed an issue that could cause instance animations to be improperly offset
[/list]

notes.title: Old-school 2D Side-scrolling Action Game Steel Sword Story Released!
notes.content:
Today we were finally able to release the Pixel Game Maker MV-created sword & sorcery action title Steel Sword Story!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34011329/65a25c20662885c9be8f34c1a456bf0078161309.gif[/img]

Here we'd like to introduce you to some of the awesome characters you'll meet in the game.

[h1]■Azul Palan Brau[/h1]
The story's hero. Former Aurum Kingdom Imperial Guard. A skilled young swordsman, he was wrongfully accused of a crime and exiled. Some say that it was his love for the princess that angered the king.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34011329/94343aaacfaa66def62013b3a5774f0204a5af68.gif[/img]

[h1]■Prime Minister Rufus[/h1]
The prime minister handling the daily affairs of Aurum Kingdom in place of King Ouro. His political skills, both externally and behind closed doors, are excellent, but his origins are a mystery.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34011329/890f6a2d77fce7be45a133dca8d1599a7d98bae0.gif[/img]

[h1]■Rose[/h1]
Princess of Aurum Kingdom. Against her father's wishes, she has fallen in love with Azul, the Imperial Guardsman who has been protecting her since childhood.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34011329/619baf0c1dcf985065343b6c4136c7086637526e.gif[/img]

[h1]■Ouro III[/h1]
King of Aurum Kingdom. Extremely strict, but not cruel. Somewhat naïve due to inheriting the throne in a time of peace, this naivete is taken advantage of by Rufus.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34011329/6650cb78c35135ed4a8d76c5c6fd65268bfe528d.gif[/img]

[h1]■Minotus[/h1]
Bull demons summoned from the demon world by Rufus. Their jump and squash attack is powerful enough to raise the ground. Be careful not to get hit by the flames they spit from their mouths.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34011329/53accd0444bab5f46fee52c0999235482ac62b5e.gif[/img]

These are the guys and girls who will be appearing in the game and providing the story with its heart and soul.
We really just can't get over these painstakingly crafted pixel graphics, and we're sure you're gonna dig them, too!

We'll be back soon with more character introductions, so stay tuned!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34011329/b943fe75446c7c65a2f43ab2888eee5c040196e2.gif[/img]

notes.title: Pixel Game Maker MV REMIX Game Jam - Winners!
notes.content:
After hosting the REMIX Game Jam and hosting [url=https://blog.playism-games.com/pixel-game-maker-mv-remix-game-jam-community-voting/]community voting[/url] for the 3 finalists, we are excited to announce our two winners!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8438467/e1b9ce84b33899c2e45646b276acd6bd062d0b5f.png[/img]

We want to take this moment to thank everyone for their efforts for joining in the week long Game Jam, and for submitting a great variety of games. We enjoyed playing through all your games, and it was a difficult choice to select the finalists. We hope that you will all continue to support Pixel Game Maker MV, and continue to take part in our future activities.

After allowing the community to choose one of the winners through community voting from the three finalists, the staff behind Pixel Game Maker MV got to choose the second winner. As promised, the two winners for our REMIX Game Jam will have their titles shown on the Pixel Game Maker MV booth at [url=https://bitsummit.org/]“BitSummit 7 Spirits”[/url], scheduled to be held in June 2019.


[h1]And the winners are....[/h1]

[b]Community Choice:[/b] Hex Hunter by Name User	
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8438467/7865d927f25995937caef8d066d9684a281222df.png[/img]

[i]PGMMV Staff Comment:[/i]
The community’s voice was overwhelming: Hex Hunter is your favorite! A twin-stick game with some intriguing concepts, we hope to see it finished some day!


[b]Pixel Game Maker MV Staff Choice:[/b] Explorer Thief by Kyle
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8438467/0df504765d8719c025a137699adbe9b8b21622bd.png[/img]

[i]PGMMV Staff Comment:[/i]
Based on the Explorer sample assets, we were quite pleased to see a stealth mechanic implemented in Pixel Game Maker MV! We hope that this project also gets continued!


Thank you again to everyone for submitting, and we look forward to more amazing games that you build in Pixel Game Maker MV!

notes.content:
Hi All,

Thank you very much for using Pixel Game Maker MV.
We have just released the ver. 0.9.5 update.
Additionally, the previous beta release, 0.9.4.2, has been moved over to the default branch.

[h1]Vote for your favourite REMIX Game Jam Game![/h1]
We are currently hosting a community vote for the best [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/837510/announcements/detail/1768134376972571540]REMIX Game Jam entry![/url] Head on over to the Playism blog to check out the entries. 
Download, play and vote for your favourite! Voting closes April 22nd! 

[url=https://blog.playism-games.com/pixel-game-maker-mv-remix-game-jam-community-voting/]Pixel Game Maker MV REMIX Game Jam - Community Voting[/url]


[h1]■Updates[/h1]

[h1]Additions[/h1]
[list]
 [*] When building a project with encryption, audio files are now also encrypted
 [*]Added additional debug commands when test playing. Can now pause play, adjust game speed, and apply a framerate limit using the new Performance/Speed Settings menu
 [*] Added ability to reverse direction for circular Courses
 [*] All error log reports should now contain a dump file as well
 [*] Added new option to save on test play 
 [*] Added additional functions to convert data imported from Sprite Studio
 [*] Added "Stop Upward Movement on Wall Collision" checkboxes to Object "Jumping and Landing Parameters"
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
 [*] Fixed bug that resulted in physics Objects not being affected by the "Change Game Speed" runtime action
 [*] Fixed bug that would cause a crash if an Object did not have an animation set and an effect for "Received Damage" is enabled
 [*] Fixed a bug that prevented the Field of Vision settings from being applied properly
 [*] Fixed bug causing text displayed using the "Display and parent-child relationship" function to be deleted when touching another Object's wall collision area
 [*] Fixed a bug that prevented correct movement if a negative value is set for the "Initial Jump Speed" setting 
 [*] Fixed a bug that caused Objects to take double damage when moving as the result of certain Template Move settings
 [*] Fixed bug that causes a crash when transitioning to a Scene that has a background with the Play Movie runtime action
 [*] Fixed bug that prevented the music from resetting properly during test play

[h1]Game Jam Submissions[/h1]
[olist][*]For the Remix Game Jam, assets from the sample games already available in Pixel Game Maker MV must be used to create a new “remixed” project.

[*]The assets are the resources in the sample project folders and include animations (motion, particle and effects) sprite sheets, tile sets, images, background music, sound effects and fonts.
Note: Assets for "Dungeon of Nazarick" are excluded from this game jam.

[*]The “remixed project” must use assets from sample projects included in Pixel Game Maker MV, but the participant’s own original assets (e.g.: new scenes, new attacks, new gameplay mechanics, etc) can be used as well.

[*]Assets created by the participants, assets with a free license, or assets purchased can also be used in the “remixed project”. However, such assets found to be in violation of copyright and/or trademark laws, and/or assets found to encroach on the rights of others may not be used.

[*]If using external assets such as those mentioned directly above, these assets cannot comprise more than 50% of your game. This is in order to maintain the “remix” concept of this contest.

[*]All participants must include in their entry folder a file including:
a.	Instructions on how to play the game;
b.	A complete list of all assets used, both from sample games and external assets.

[*]There are no specific requirements when it comes to type (top view or side view) or genre of the game. Be creative!

[*]Entries should be created and worked on during the dates specified for this contest.

[*]Submissions are limited to one project per entry. However, multiple entries are allowed.

notes.title: Making 64-bit the Default
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

First of all, thank you for your support during this Early Access period: we've really managed to improve a lot over the last few months, and we have a lot more improvements coming!

We announced with the release of the 0.9.4 update that we are going to be switching the default version of Pixel Game Maker MV to the 64-bit version. This has been decided in accordance with our plans for further improvements to Pixel Game Maker MV.

[b]The switch will occur on Thursday, February 14 at 3 AM GMT.[/b]

Our reasons for this change are as follows:

[list]
[*] The 64-bit version is, in most cases, faster and generally more stable than the 32-bit version.
[*] Looking at the information available to us, almost everyone is running a 64-bit OS.
[/list]

And after months of testing the 64-bit with you all, we feel comfortable that this will result in generally a better experience for those who have not yet tried the 64-bit version from the Beta tab.

If you have any comments about this change, please let us know in the comments or on Twitter!

For users who are still on a 32-bit operating system, the 32-bit version will still be available via a branch on the Steam Beta tab.
This can be accessed via the following method:

[h1]Switching to 32-bit Build:[/h1]
1. Open "Properties" for Pixel Game Maker MV in your Steam Library, and select the "BETAS" tab.
2. Select "32bit" from the drop down menu and close Properties.

notes.title: Ver. 0.9.3 Update (Open Beta) and Restructuring of the Roadmap for Future Development
notes.content:
Hi All,

Thank you very much for using Pixel Game Maker MV.
We have just released the ver. 0.9.3 update.

[h1]■Updates[/h1]

[h1]Additions[/h1]
[list]
 [*] Screen Area Movement Restriction Settings have been added to Objects under the Add Object Settings Item list
 [*] Added "Group Management" function to Settings menu. Up to 31 different group types can be created, for Objects and Tiles.
Additionally, all related Group and Tile settings have been updated to reflect support for additional Groups.
 [*]Added "Edit Base Object" to the right-click menu for Object placed in a scene (placed Object list)
 [*]Added "Load a File" to Other Runtime Actions.
 [*]Added "Variation" parameter to Object Basic Settings. A non-zero value will enable a randomized damage spread.
 [*]Added intermediate color setting to particle effect parameters
 [*]Added neutral color parameters for particles.
 [*] Added the "Fantasy SideView" and "Fantasy TopView" projects, created specially for Pixel Game Maker MV by famed RPG Maker asset creator Takumi Naramura of NIGORO. Please check out the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/835430/LaMulana_2/]LA-MULANA series[/url] if you get the chance!
[/list]
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32941247/8a3c94ec5f55516f9ba2e40b80a90ebfe2606fe6.jpg[/img]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
 [*] Fixed issue where the auto-scroll function could scroll outside of the valid display area
 [*] Fixed issue where displaying a filter immediately before a different filter ends would also end both filters
 [*] Fixed the issue causing the debug "Execution Log" to display the non-localized name
 [*] Fixed an issue that could cause Object to have the incorrect coordinates
 [*] Fixed an issue that was preventing the "Contact with Tile's Wall Detection When Moving One Tile" from working as intended
 [*] Fixed an issue that caused the debug functions to not be displayed properly during test play after changing an object's scale
 [*] Fixed an issue where objects that are not supposed to be knockedback could be moved
 [*] Fixed an issue where mouse wheel scrolling could become reversed when using the Scene tool
 [*] Fixed an issue involving changing a variable using debug functionality not working as intended
 [*] Fixed Object shaking when "Fix Relative Position to Camera" is enabled
 [*] Fixed an issue where the "Set Distance" setting for the "Distance with Attack Detection" Link Condition was not working as intended
 [*] Fixed an issue where Locking on Attack Detection would sometimes not function as intended
 [*] Fixed a number of issues related to Saving and Loading from file
 [*] Fixed an issue a Link wouldn't function when all "Other Condition Settings" are disabled even though other Link Conditions are fulfilled
 [*] Fixed an issue where sound effects wouldn't playback when using the Overlap settings
 [*] Fixed an issue that could cause the Player to crash if the Default Menu Screen for a Scene has been deleted
 [*] Fixed an issue that could cause Layers to not be displayed and then a crash when changing Scenes
 [*] Fixed an issue where the Area Accessible settings for both Player and Camera would not update after changing the project's resolition setting
 [*] Fixed an issue that could cause Runtime Actions involving Menu scenes to stop functioning after adjusting Menu scene tab order
 [*] Fixed assorted issues involving Actions that cause Menu scenes to update what is displayed on screen
 [*] Fixed memory issue that occurred when using the Plug-in tool to select an object via the Preview tab
 [*] Fixed an issue where the "Move in Reverse Direction" for "Move Towards Display Direction" was sometimes not working as intended
 [*] Fixed an issue where an Object that was stopped with a Template Move Settings would not turn
 [*] Fixed an issue where changing the Game Speed for multiple Objects simulaneously would not work as expected
 [*] Fixed an issue where the display of Trad. Chinese and Simpl. Chinese were reversed
 [*] Fixed an issue where animation effects generated by a Gimmick Tile might not display correctly
 [*] Fixed an issue where Tank and Vehicle movement types were not affected by changing the game speed
 [*] Fixed an issue where the "Increase/Decrease Object Move Speed" was not working as intended for some Objects
 [*] Fixed an issue where Objects using the "Rotate and Auto-generate" setting would not stop movement
 [*] Fixed an issue where using the "Move Object" Action while an object is falling could result in the object teleporting
 [*] Fixed an issue that could cause the Player to crash when playing a video
 [*] Fixed an issue where using "Move Layer" at the same time as certain other Runtime Actions would cause a crash
 [*] Fixed an issue where Objects that were affected by "Move Layer" and "Destroy Object" simultaneously would spawn multiple copies when that Object is restored
[/list]

[h1]Changes/Adjustments[/h1]
[list]
 [*] Visiblity of an opaque Object that is overlapped by a semi-transparent object in the same Layer has been adjusted
 [*] The functioning of Runtime Action "Push/Pull Object" has been adjusted
 [*] Collision with a horizontal or vertical Slope has been adjusted
 [*] Coordinate positions of two overlapping Objects that both have "Not Pushed Back" enabled should properly be maintained now
 [*]Updated the "Show Text" Action to add note regarding decimal place support
 [*] Adjusted Portal Transfer settings to prevent objects from being selected while adjusting Portal placement
 [*]The Link Condition "Distance with Other Objects" has had the "Set Distance" function adjusted.
 [*] The "Lock Object" Action's "Set by Object Group" has been adjusted to unify handling when the Group includes the acting Object
 [*] Adjusted the "Shoot at the Selected On-screen Object Groups" setting so that it won't select previously fired bullets of the same type.
 [*]Revised wording of bullet limit setting to clarify how it limits the bullet count.
 [*]Adjusted the "Change Game Speed" Action to also affect Objects that are generated while the speed change is in effect.
 [*]Adjusted some of the text in the Tutorial.
 [*]Adjusted memory handling for the 64-bit version of the Editor.
 [*]Removed unnecessary Transition when performing Save and Load operations as long as the start and end scenes are the same.
 [*]Improved performance when frequently updating displayed text
 [*]Updated some UI elements
[/list]

Please be sure to give it a try in the 64-bit version as well.

With regard to future updates, we are currently in the process of restructuring our development roadmap to reflect the many requests we’ve received from our users since the Early Access release.

[h1]■Development Schedule[/h1]
First off, we’re prioritizing consideration and implementation of requests and adjustments related to the “enhancement of freedom”.

We also plan on adding a wide variety of features and functions to help further simplify and diversify the game creation process, such as the widely-requested functions for action-RPGs and a “roguelike” theme focusing on random generation features, and more.

Additionally, in order to further reduce the processing load for the player, we are also currently considering a large-scale overhaul to ensure that we can provide the smoothest and most comfortable experience possible.

Of course, in the meantime, we’ll be implementing other updates based on user feedback as well, specifically focusing on improving UI usability and general improvements for beginners in particular. We’re looking forward to receiving even more feedback from our users in order to continue improving and enhancing both the software itself and the user experience.

We apologize for the ongoing wait for the full release, but we hope you can bear with us. In the meantime, look forward to all kinds of new and cool updates and additions to Pixel Game Maker MV!

[h1]Full Release[/h1]
The previously released Open Beta version has been fully released.

notes.title: Pixel Game Maker MV 64-bit Version! (Open Beta)
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

We are excited to announce the release of the [b]64-bit version of Pixel Game Maker MV[/b] to a new beta branch that is available now.

The beta 64-bit version gives Pixel Game Maker MV access to more memory and makes it better use modern processors. This means you should have less stuttering, less memory-related crashes and just a more stable and smoother experience overall when creating your games.

Please do understand that this version is in a beta stage and we offer it as an option to anyone that would like to try it out.

To make the switch, you can follow these steps:
[olist]
    [*]Open "Properties" for Pixel Game Maker MV in your Steam Library;
    [*]Select the "Beta" tab;
    [*]Select the option "open_beta64"
[/olist]

Switching to the 64-bit version will not affect your project data, and you can switch back to 32-bit 0.9.2 (open beta) or the default 0.9.1 without worry. Should you wish to revert to the 0.9.1 32-bit version, you can simply choose "NONE - Opt out of all beta programs" and to go back to the 0.9.2 32-bit version you can select the "open_beta" option.

notes.title: New Project: Recreate LA-MULANA 2!
notes.content:
Using Pixel Game Maker MV, we've taken the liberty of recreating the Ratatoskr mid-boss battle from the popular Steam title La-Mulana 2!
The animations in La-Mulana 2 were created using the [url=https://www.webtech.co.jp/eng/spritestudio/]OPTPiX SpriteStudio[/url]  animation production software, and we were able to recreate the La-Mulana 2 animations by feeding the data into Pixel Game Maker MV.

Check out the below image to see how faithful our recreation is to the original:

We will also be unveiling a playable version of the recreated Ratatoskr battle at Digital Games Expo 2018, held in Akihabara on November 4th. The event will also feature a talk session in which you can hear some behind-the-scenes stories on development as well.

We are also currently planning some opportunities for overseas fans to get their hands on some playable samples and check out various projects at some point in the near future, so be sure to stay tuned for further info!

[h1]About La-Mulana 2[/h1]
La-Mulana 2 features sprawling ancient ruins, mind-boggling mysteries, untold numbers of items, and terrible enemies combining to form what is possibly the perfect Metroidvania-style "archaeological ruin exploration action game".

notes.title: How Pixel Game Maker MV Came To Be
notes.content:
Early Access for Pixel Game Maker MV is just over the horizon. Today, we'd like to share with everyone a message from the producers detailing just how the game came to be!

[b]The Birth of Pixel Game Maker MV[/b]
Steam is home to many hit titles created using the RPG Maker series, such as To The Moon, etc.
https://store.steampowered.com/app/206440/To_the_Moon/

However, when checking out trends among the various games sold on Steam, we saw that action games were really pulling in a lot of fans. We feel that this is thanks to the fact that, with Steam games available all over the world, language barrier doesn't tend to be an issue, and players from around the globe find it easy to enjoy action games.

This got us hoping that releasing Pixel Game Maker MV just might encourage players to create even more Maker series games, and so we jumped right into development.

[b]Main Features[/b]
While there certainly are a large number of settings and buttons, etc., we're doing our best to ensure that Pixel Game Maker MV is as easy to use as possible. The software allows for the import of new assets and materials, so importing the assets scheduled to be made available on the official website should help provide some great ideas for animation settings and more.

Additionally, we've included all-new features such as physics and co-op/multiplayer battle play, further increasing the possibilities for the types of games you can create.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Btd0_qTzZgQ

Once you get the hang of the software, you'll be able to create amazing games without any coding required, with virtually no limits but your own imagination. The sample games we've made available were created by a single graphic designer, so be sure to check out some of the things that are possible with Pixel Game Maker MV!
